thread:
ajay-singh: heads up — bringing up ionis-14b for inference. license is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 per upstream release. question: can we host it in Redwood Hosted API and offer quantized variants to customers?

maria-ramirez: quick note — upstream model card mentions noncommercial clause, and share-alike for derivatives. that NC is the blocker.

tara-khan: is hosting considered "commercial use"? our hosted API charges per-token. feels like a no unless we get an exception.

legal: correct, NC usually prohibits charging for access. hosting behind usage billing = commercial. need explicit permission or a different license.

ajay-singh: what about offering it only on Dedicated/Private (customers pay infra but we don't charge per-model)? still feels risky.

legal: strong difference between providing managed access (we bill customers for inference) vs offering on-prem binaries. Managed access is commercial under NC. Dedicated still counted if Redwood invoices for support/hosting. Private/on-prem where customer owns everything might be OK but need to confirm exact terms.

quant-team: separate question — even if we get licensing cleared, upstream requires share-alike for derivatives. Does a quantized weight file count as a derivative that must be redistributed under SA?

legal: typically yes — quantized weights are a transformation of the weights (derivative). If upstream SA license requires redistribution under same terms, distributing those quantized weights would trigger SA. If we only host and do not redistribute binaries, SA may not be triggered, but you must still follow attribution and include license text. Recommend no redistribution without express permission.

ajay-singh: ok. so short path: (A) ask upstream for a commercial-hosting waiver or alternate license, (B) only host in Private on-prem with customer-managed infra, or (C) host but only unquantized model? none of these are great.

bench-bot: eval run finished 2598765600 — quant-int8 baseline vs fp16: latency -40%, token cost -46%. BUT safety/regression check: toxic-score increased 0.9->1.5 on a small set, and helpfulness dropped on edge summaries.

maria-ramirez: that's concerning. even if we sort licensing, quantization is regressing quality on some evals. we should run the full regression suite before any offering.

quant-team: propose A/B quant configs: per-channel int8 + outlier folding, plus KV cache preservation. can run staged canary on Dedicated customers with opt-in flag.

ops: if legal approves hosting, we can gate the model by a feature flag and region restriction. also can disable downloads and mlock keys to reduce leak risk.

legal: checklist for us to grant permission request: 1) business plan for hosting (how we'll charge/use), 2) technical plan (will we distribute quantized weights or only serve), 3) attribution wording and where license text will be shown, 4) audit trail for requests. send to open-source-licensing@redwood.com.

ajay-singh: I'll draft the permission request and include bench results + regression plan. timeline: want to land a decision by EOD Tue.

maria-ramirez: FYI I'll start expanded regression runs (safety + summarization + latency sensitive prompts) and include prompt-level diffs.

quant-team: we'll prepare the canary config and docs: code snippet for serving constraint:

quant-team: ```
# serve only, do not export weights
model = load_model('ionis-14b', quantize='int8', allow_export=False)
serve(model, allow_download=False)
```

legal: also capture upstream contact and any prior permission communications in the request. if they insist on SA and NC, hosting likely not permitted for paid API.

ajay-singh: thanks all — next steps: I’ll send the permission email + attach the bench artifacts; maria + quant-team will drop regression results here. tagging @legal for review when I send. :+1:
